nodes.name: Hydrothermal Ni2(OH)2CO3 synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ni(NO3)2 (0.9 g), NH4F (0.23 g), and urea (0.9 g) were dissolved in 75 mL of deionized (DI) water to form a reaction solution. Then, the solution was transferred to a Teflon-lined steel autoclave, and the autoclave was placed in an oven at 120 °C for 8 h. After natural cooling, the sample was rinsed thoroughly with DI water.

nodes.source_text: In the first step, Ni2(OH)2CO3 nanosheet arrays were obtained by a one-step hydrothermal method using commercial nickel foam as the substrate. For this, Ni(NO3)2 (0.9 g), NH4F (0.23 g), and urea (0.9 g) were dissolved in 75 mL of deionized (DI) water... at 120 °C for 8 h. After natural cooling, the sample was rinsed thoroughly with DI water.

nodes.name: ALD TiO2 coating
nodes.procedure: The prepared Ni2(OH)2CO3 nanosheet arrays were placed in an ALD reactor (ALD PICOSUN P-300F) along with TiCl4 and H2O as the Ti and O source, respectively. Then, TiO2 was deposited at 120 °C for 140 cycles. Argon was used as the carrier gas.

unit_operations.name: ALD deposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: TiO2 was deposited at 120 °C for 140 cycles. Argon was used as the carrier gas.

nodes.source_text: the prepared Ni2(OH)2CO3 nanosheet arrays were placed in an ALD reactor (ALD PICOSUN P-300F) along with TiCl4 and H2O as the Ti and O source, respectively. Then, TiO2 was deposited at 120 °C for 140 cycles.

nodes.name: Low-temperature sulfurization
nodes.procedure: The obtained TiO2@Ni2(OH)2CO3 nanoflake array samples were transferred to a 0.1 M Na2S solution and heated at 90 °C for 9 h. After natural cooling and rinsing with DI water, the TiO2@Ni3S2 core/branch arrays were obtained.

nodes.name: Direct Ni3S2 synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ni2(OH)2CO3 nanosheet arrays on nickel foam (without the ALD TiO2 step) were sulfurized using the same sulfurization conditions: transferred to a 0.1 M Na2S solution and heated at 90 °C for 9 h.
nodes.source_text: For comparison, Ni3S2 nanofake arrays were also synthesized by the direct sulfurization of the Ni2(OH)2CO3 nanosheet arrays on nickel foam (without the ALD TiO2 step) using the same sulfurization conditions...

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show TiO2@Ni3S2 core/branch arrays with cross-linked Ni3S2 nanoflake branches of 10–15 nm thickness coating the TiO2 core, preserving porous morphology with ~1 μm height.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the internal TiO2 core is homogeneously coated by the cross-linked Ni3S2 nanoflake shell with 10–15 nm thickness (Fig. 1c, f).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows TiO2 core covered by cross-linked Ni3S2 nanoflake branches; SAED confirms polycrystalline rings of (001), (101), (110), (021) planes of Ni3S2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the TiO2 core is homogeneously covered by cross-linked Ni3S2 nanofakes (Fig. 2a). A clear interplanar d-spacing of ∼0.71 nm is observed... SAED pattern shows polycrystalline difraction rings of the TiO2@Ni3S2 sample (Fig. 2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM along [100] zone axis shows Ni3S2 interplanar d-spacings of 0.24 nm (003) and 0.23 nm (021) planes with 70° angle between facets, confirming exposed {210̄} high-index facets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the interplanar d-spacing of 0.24 and 0.23 nm matched well with the (003) and (021) planes of the hexagonal Ni3S2 phase... the angle between the (003) and (021) facets is approximately 70°, which corresponds to the theoretical value of 70.8°.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS maps confirm uniform distribution of O, S, Ni, and Ti elements in TiO2@Ni3S2 arrays.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) maps (Fig. 2e) confrm the presence and uniform distribution of O, S, Ni, and Ti in the TiO2@Ni3S2 arrays.

nodes.characterization_summary: TiO2@Ni3S2 branch arrays show specific surface area of 4.623 m²/g, significantly higher than common Ni3S2 arrays at 1.594 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The common Ni3S2 arrays and TiO2@Ni3S2 branch nanosheet arrays show specifc surface areas of 1.594 and 4.623 m² g⁻¹, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms high-purity Ni3S2 phase (JCPDS 44-1418) in TiO2@Ni3S2 with strong (021) and (003) peaks; amorphous TiO2 shows no peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the difraction peaks that can be indexed well with the Ni3S2 phase (JCPDS 44-1418)... strong difraction peaks of (021) and (003) plane can be observed clearly.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Ni3S2 characteristic peaks at ~203, 223, 305, 348 cm⁻¹ and amorphous TiO2 peak at ~150 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TiO2@Ni3S2 arrays show fve characteristic peaks at ~203, 223, 305, and 348 cm⁻¹, which match well with those of the Ni3S2 phase. The characteristic peak at ∼150 cm⁻¹ could be indexed well with that of amorphous TiO2.

Two main core levels (Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/2) that are characteristic of the Ni state in Ni3S2 are located at 873.28 and 855.78 eV... S 2p spectra, two characteristic peaks are detected at 163.28 eV (S 2p1/2) and 161.28 eV (S 2p3/2)... Ti 2p1/2 (463.85 eV) and Ti 2p3/2 (458.0 eV)... O 1s spectra, which could be indexed well with Ti–O and O–H bonds, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at various scan rates yields Cdl of 42 mF cm⁻² for TiO2@Ni3S2, higher than Ni2(OH)2CO3 (24 mF cm⁻²) and Ni3S2 (29 mF cm⁻²), indicating larger ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the TiO2@Ni3S2 electrode possesses a high capacitance, up to 42 mF cm⁻², which is much higher than those of Ni2(OH)2CO3 (24 mF cm⁻²) and Ni3S2 (29 mF cm⁻²) electrodes.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows TiO2@Ni3S2 has smallest Rct and Rs of 1.45 Ω among compared electrodes, indicating fastest charge transfer kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the TiO2@Ni3S2 electrode shows the smallest Rct value among the three electrodes... the solution resistance (Rs) values of Ni2(OH)2CO3, Ni3S2, and TiO2@Ni3S2 electrodes are 1.49, 1.46, and 1.45 Ω, respectively.
